issues.legal_issue: A village self-government body has standing to seek constitutional review of an order that nullifies its statutory action taken in the exercise of its public functions.
material_facts: The village body considered residents’ complaints about construction that allegedly obstructed access to a well and chapel and affected the flow of rainwater.
The village body revoked an occupancy certificate and cancelled construction permission, later recalling the cancellation after recognizing that natural justice had not been followed.
The village head issued a notice directing the company to stop further construction, and the village body rejected the company’s request to use the property as a guest house.
An authority hearing the company’s appeals set aside the village body’s resolutions and the village head’s notice.
The village body filed constitutional petitions challenging those orders, and the High Court dismissed the petitions as not maintainable.
issues.conclusion: The village body had standing to file the writ petitions, and the High Court erred in dismissing them as not maintainable. The petitions were restored for decision on their merits.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 226 and 227 permit a body whose legal interests are affected to seek review of an authority’s order. Article 40 and Part IX of the Constitution, including Articles 243(d) and 243G, inform the understanding of a Panchayat as a representative institution of self-government. The Goa Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, including Sections 60, 62, 64, 66 and 178, assigns the Panchayat and its Sarpanch public functions and powers; the Court also referred to Section 8 on the Panchayat’s corporate status. The Court applied Karunagappally Grama Panchayat v. State of Kerala, High Court of M.P. v. Mahesh Prakash, State of Orissa v. Union of India, and Godde Venkateswara Rao v. Government of Andhra Pradesh, which support standing where an entity’s own legal interests or functions are affected by an order.

rule.if: local_self_government_body_challenges_authority_order and body_exercised_public_functions and authority_nullified_body_action and body_legal_interests_affected

predicates.local_self_government_body_challenges_au: A body established to represent a local community seeks constitutional review of an order made by another authority.
predicates.body_exercised_public_functions: The local body or its officer acted in carrying out public functions assigned to the body.
predicates.authority_nullified_body_action: The authority’s order set aside or nullified an action taken by the local body or its officer.
predicates.body_legal_interests_affected: The authority’s order affected the local body’s own legal interests or its ability to carry out its public functions.

issues.definition: When a local self-government body seeks review of an authority’s order nullifying its public action and that order affects the body’s legal interests, its writ petition is maintainable.
